Sasikiran, Svane and Vogel reach the podium after exciting final round

Indian GM Krishnan Sasikiran won the 29th Open International Bavarian Chess Championship, which concluded on Sunday in Gmund am Tegernsee. The nine-round Swiss tournament, held at Gut Kaltenbrunn from 31 October to 8 November, attracted 548 participants.

Sasikiran finished with 7½/9 points, the same score as German GMs Frederik Svane and Roven Vogel and Indian FM Arun Daakshin. The title was decided by the first tiebreak criterion, the average rating of opponents, which favoured Sasikiran. Svane finished second, Vogel third and Daakshin fourth.

The situation atop the standings changed considerably in Saturday's penultimate round, when top seed Svane defeated G.N. Gopal with the white pieces. Alexander Donchenko, Leonardo Costa, Roven Vogel and several other contenders also collected full points, leaving nine players tied for first place on 6½/8 going into the final round. Sasikiran remained among the leaders after drawing with second seed Jaime Santos.

Sunday's decisive encounters produced an unusual result: Black won on each of the top four boards. Sasikiran, playing black against German IM Adrian Gschnitzer on board four, obtained attacking chances on the kingside. His opponent's decision to close the centre on move 20 allowed the Indian GM to build up pressure without facing sufficient counterplay. A blunder on move 25 was met by the refutation: a rook sacrifice on f3. Gschnitzer resigned soon after.

With the best tiebreak score among the leaders, Sasikiran knew that a victory would guarantee him first place regardless of the other results. The 45-year-old from Chennai finished the tournament with a performance rating of 2675.
Adrian Gschnitzer facing Krishnan Sasikiran | Photo: Sandra Schmidt

On the top board, Svane had a rather different experience against Turkish IM Eray Kilic. Playing black in the Exchange Variation of the French Defence, the top seed initially had little to work with in a symmetrical position. Kilic, who needed only a draw to secure his final GM norm, defended accurately for much of the encounter. The game eventually reached a rook endgame in which both players had passed pawns, but Kilic made a mistake in the ensuing pawn race. Svane converted his advantage after 92 moves, securing second place while denying his opponent the norm.

Third place went to 26-year-old German GM Roven Vogel, who defeated compatriot Alexander Donchenko with the black pieces. The players reached a typical King's Indian structure, with white advancing on the queenside and Black seeking counterplay against the king. Donchenko declined a repetition of moves shortly before the time control, despite being short of time. The complications that followed eventually favoured Vogel, a former world under-16 champion, who finished with 7½ points.

The fourth player to reach that score was 17-year-old Indian FM Arun Daakshin. Rated 2341 at the start of the event, Daakshin defeated reigning German champion Leonardo Costa on board three. Costa's ambitious play on the kingside allowed his opponent to establish a strong knight in the centre, while Daakshin subsequently opened lines against the white king on the queenside. The victory gave the Indian youngster fourth place in the final standings.

Gopal, who had led outright after round six, recovered from his loss to Svane by defeating American IM Evan Park in the final round. He finished fifth with 7/9 points, ahead of Rithvik Raja, Elham Amar and English IM Sohum Lohia, who also scored 7 points. Donchenko and Costa, meanwhile, ended the tournament with 6½ points following their final-round defeats.

Among the other notable results, Polish IM Klaudia Kulon finished as the highest-placed woman with 6½ points, ahead of German WGM Kateryna Dolzhykova on tiebreaks. Svenja Butenandt took third place in the women's standings with six points and secured a WIM norm after drawing with GM Mathias Womacka in the final round.

Indian youngster S Midilesh M also achieved an IM norm, defeating Georg Seul in the last round to finish on 6½ points. In the senior category, 62-year-old IM Dieter Morawietz took first place on tiebreaks with 6 points, ahead of Mathias Womacka and Martin Forchert.
